> **Capability note.** The `fathom verify` gate itself is fully
> harness-agnostic — it's a git-native/CLI check, identical whether Codex or
> Claude Code (or a human) runs it, so nothing below is a Codex compromise.
> This file is the DEPRECATED custom-prompts twin
> (`~/.codex/prompts/fathom-verify.md`, `/prompts:fathom-verify`; written
> only by `fathom init --skills=codex-prompts`). `fathom init --skills=codex`
> writes the skill proper to `.agents/skills/fathom-verify/SKILL.md`, the
> path Codex documents — prefer it.

Run the gate:

```sh
fathom verify --service $SERVICE --plan $PLAN
```

- `--service` required; `--plan` repeatable.
- HTTP mode by default (`--url`, default `http://localhost:7575` or
  `$FATHOM_HTTP`); pass `--store <path>` for direct mode against a
  `.sqlite`/`.db` file, bypassing the daemon — what CI should do.
- `--strict`: claimed-but-`Unknown` tasks also fail. Always use in CI.
- `--require-all`: the wave gate — additionally fails on any open/
  in-progress task.
- `--concern <name>` scopes contradiction checking; `--json` for machine
  output; `--quiet-pass` suppresses output on a passing gate.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | every claimed task verified | proceed |
| `1` | a claimed task failed | real failure — fix the code or uncheck the box, never just re-run |
| `2` | operational (daemon unreachable / service not indexed / empty index) | fail-open — not a verdict on the plan; ingest and retry |

Pre-push: fail-open on 2, block only on 1. CI: build its own store and treat
2 as a failure too (a live daemon should never be a CI dependency).

**Empty index ≠ all claims false.** If every task looks like it's failing,
check whether the service has any symbols at all (`list_services` MCP tool,
or `fathom inspect --service $SERVICE`) before assuming the plan is wrong —
a genuinely empty index is exit 2, an operational problem.

**`test_reaches` ≠ `runtime_pass`.** A pass means a `Test*` statically
reaches the symbol via the call graph — never that the test runs or passes.

## Computed progress

```sh
fathom plans status --service $SERVICE   # per-plan rollup: proven / claimed-unproven / open / deferred / other-skipped
fathom plans next   --service $SERVICE   # ordered work frontier, each row's {symbol, package} anchor
```

Both are derived from the index every time — never an asserted state. A
"no open work" from `plans next` is a plan CI will actually pass.
